calibration: Shipped expert placement and draft vocabulary for each model file.
method: Each server handled one warm-up and nine fresh requests. The tables give the median of three requests per workload. Each timed request read 4,096 prompt tokens and requested 256 output tokens. The server reported zero cached prompt tokens for every timed request. Rates use the engine timers. The per-request record also gives elapsed time at the client.
token_hash: SHA-256 over signed 32-bit token IDs in little-endian order.

passed_checks: output equality at three expert residency settings
repeatable optional fast prefill at three chunk sizes
accepted copy and three wrong copies preserve the prompt checkpoint and next tokens
output equality at three expert residency settings
repeatable optional fast prefill at three chunk sizes
accepted copy and three wrong copies preserve the prompt checkpoint and next tokens

verification_only_iq3_s.method: The target checked 255 known consecutive output tokens per request with eight positions per full window. Supplying the correct proposals took zero measured time.

additional_requests_method: The benchmark text generator produced one extra 4,096-token prompt of each kind from seed 201. The earlier experimental generator also used these prompts. Each rate is one observation.
post_commit_requests_method: The benchmark generator drew a new seed after the final engine commit. Each build then handled three fresh prompts from that seed on each model file.
prompt_profile_method: One 4,096-token code review prompt in one chunk with 16,500 resident experts. GPU events timed each stage. The 2,000 prompt tokens/s goal allows 2,048 ms in total.

wide_verification_only_iq3_s.method: A separate test build used the exact prompt matrix products to compute vocabulary scores for every trial position. It consumed a known-correct continuation and checked all 255 token IDs. Each measurement used the first request of a workload. Proposal time and rejection recovery are excluded.

exact_weight_tests.rank_method: Gaussian elimination over the prime 65,521 on a 320-by-320 minor of each mixer in layers 0, 23 and 47.

routed_projection_reuse.method: Sixteen equally spaced rows in each of 512 experts were compared for each of the three projections in layers 0, 23, and 47. The program compared the entire decoded weight rows and four 32-weight slices per row. Each slice was compared at the same input coordinate within its projection. Signed zeros were treated as equal.

native_prompt_copy_experiment_iq3_s.method: The native generator on IQ3_S used 16,500 resident experts. It proposed tokens only from earlier input or output and used a single target token on a miss. The test timed all generation after the first output. It checked the 256 output token IDs against v0.4.0 after generation. Each arm kept its model loaded across four requests. This path ran outside the server.

long_copy_method: A buffered greedy request can check a matching passage in one block of up to 256 positions. The target scores every position. It restores the prior state after a wrong proposal. When the generated text has already changed an earlier matching passage, the engine uses short windows. Streaming, tool calls, custom stop strings, and sampling use the ordinary verification windows.

additional_server_checks_iq3_s.method: Eight chat requests compared the complete output text and token IDs with v0.4.0. They included a changed passage, a follow-up, a custom stop string, a streamed response, fixed-seed sampling, and two inputs longer than the draft ring.

additional_server_checks_ud_iq3_xxs.method: Eight chat requests compared the complete output text and token IDs with v0.4.0. They included a changed passage, a follow-up, a custom stop string, a streamed response, fixed-seed sampling, and two inputs longer than the draft ring.

edited_copy_pilot_iq3_s.method: A separate test library used a recent edit in an already copied passage to select short checks. Each of three real servers handled four requests. Each rate is one observation. The final implementation uses the same condition. The servers held different expert counts.

fixed_expert_count_iq3_s.method: Both real servers held exactly 14,000 experts. They used the same nine fresh 4,096-token prompts and the same 9 GiB memory floor as the automatic-placement tests.
